model_card.inputs: 17 keypoints + person box from YOLO26n-pose + ByteTrack (no video stored; face points only as head position)
model_card.windows: last 2 s at 10 fps, scored every 0.5 s; torso-scaled, pair-centred
model_card.classifier: ensemble: average of LightGBM (24 features, clipped to the training 1st-99th percentile) and a 51k-parameter 1D-CNN over the active pair's keypoint sequence; trained on full, waist-up and chest-up copies of every clip plus one-person / close-to-camera negatives
model_card.split: 15% of groups locked as a hold-out (stratified by dataset and kind) and evaluated once; tuning by GroupKFold on the other 85%; AIRTLab camera pairs kept together
model_card.threshold: alarm when the smoothed score (alpha 0.6) stays >= 0.6562 for 1.0 s with at least 2 people tracked; FIGHT_AT fixed on the training part at 9% normal-clip false alarms
failure_modes: hugs and close contact: 2 of 18 hold-out hug/clap clips raised an alarm
very short clips (SCF, ~2 s) can't hold the 1 s alarm persistence
small or distant people on CCTV: pair features often missing
weapons are not recognised as objects; only the body motion is scored
a fight where only one person is tracked can't raise FIGHT (1.7% of fight clips in training)

disclosure: Official numbers are from a second look at a hold-out set of 470 clips that no tuning, threshold or model choice ever saw. clip_* = RLVS + AIRTLab hold-out clips; cctv_domain = SCF + SCVD hold-out clips. The final model also trains on other SCF/SCVD clips, so that row is not a pure domain test: the earlier model trained without any CCTV scored AUC 0.709 on CCTV. Dataset clips are 2-5 s long, so false alarms per camera-hour are not measured yet; live-room numbers come from our own labelled footage. Practice-run lesson: 100% on KTH, zero live until retuned. We detect physical aggression from body motion only; we do not claim verbal or online bullying, weapon recognition, or night vision.
